comment.value: The paper proposes LiveVQA, the first dataset which evaluates the abilities of MLLM to answer questions about live, evolving visual information. The authors curate various latest information from youtube, news and arxiv papers, resulting in 26,988 images and 107,143 Q/As. The authors conduct comprehensive experiments benchmarking 17 state-of-the-art MLLMs, revealing significant limitations of current SOTA MLLMs that still struggle with visual knowledges beyond their training cutoffs, but performance could be significantly improved when employing search tools.

Thank you for your time and effort.

Dear Area Chair and Reviewers,

We extend our sincerest gratitude for your professional, insightful, and constructive feedback throughout the review process. Your guidance has been invaluable in helping us refine and strengthen our work. Based on your comprehensive suggestions, we have conducted extensive revisions and additional experiments to address all raised concerns. We hope that this revision adequately resolves any doubts you may have.

During the rebuttal period, we conducted the following key revisions and clarifications:

1.  **Clarification of Our Core Contribution as a "Live" Framework (Reviewers dDKo, Q8F8):** To address crucial concerns about long-term utility, we have clarified that our primary contribution is not a static dataset, but a **dynamic and automated data engine** designed for continuous, streamlined updates. This framework is our answer to the challenge of keeping a real-time benchmark relevant.

2.  **Strengthened Methodological Rigor and Transparency (Reviewers dDKo, Q8F8):** We have strengthened the paper by detailing our quality control mechanisms. This includes using the official YouTube Data API to circumvent crawling bias for videos, performing manual verification to ensure the temporal relevance of content (100% pass rate on 500 samples), and validating our LLM-as-Judge with a 300-sample manual check, which yielded 100% accuracy.

3.  **Deepened Analysis of the Benchmark's Challenge (Reviewer YJxH):** In response to an insightful question about the benchmark's difficulty, we have elaborated that knowledge updated via fine-tuning is often "fragile" and not robust to simple rephrasing. We also highlighted the inherent performance trade-off, where updating with LiveVQA harms general vision capabilities (e.g., on MMStar), revealing a critical dilemma our benchmark is designed to measure.

4.  **Clarification on Scope and Future Vision (Reviewers mcho, Q8F8):** We have clarified that while the current version is English-focused to ensure quality, a multilingual expansion to 10+ languages is a core part of our future work. To ensure long-term sustainability, we are also proactively migrating our pipeline from costly proprietary APIs to high-performance open-source models.

**Additional Enhancements:**

1.  **Expanded Baselines with State-of-the-Art Models (Reviewer YJxH):** We have expanded our experiments to include the latest SOTA models, such as Grok-4, Claude4-sonnet, and GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking. The new results reaffirm our core finding: even the most advanced models struggle with live visual knowledge, but their performance is significantly uplifted by tool-use.

2.  **Demonstrated Continuous Data Collection (Reviewer dDKo):** As direct proof of our "live" framework's capability, we have presented new data statistics showing our ongoing, high-volume data collection from May to July 2025.

We are pleased to report that our detailed responses and revisions have led Reviewer **dDKo** to raise their score to **5 (Strong Accept)**, while Reviewers **YJxH** and **Q8F8** have also expressed their satisfaction and maintained their positive ratings. We sincerely thank all reviewers again for your valuable time and expertise in reviewing our work.

We sincerely appreciate your review and valuable suggestions. We fully agree with the potential challenges and limitations you pointed out, which we also addressed in our manuscript. Here, we provide a more detailed explanation to reinforce your confidence in our work:

---

**Q1:** Could limitations from platform anti-crawling measures and interfaces lead to unexpected bias in the collected data?

**A1:** Thank you very much for highlighting this practical and crucial issue. We acknowledge that during continuous data collection from the internet, anti-crawling mechanisms deployed by various platforms may indeed introduce biases into the dataset. Our strategy for dealing with this is systematic, and deeply integrated into our long-term project commitment.
    
1. For news articles and academic papers, we recognize the challenges posed by web scraping due to anti-crawling measures. Our pipeline is modularly designed, allowing us to promptly update or replace crawlers upon detecting that existing crawlers become ineffective. As part of our annual update promise, continuous technical maintenance will become routine, thus significantly minimizing any interruptions or biases introduced by changes in anti-crawling policies.

2. For video data, our collection strategy does not rely on traditional web crawlers. As clearly described in Appendix C.2, our video data is sourced directly through the official YouTube Data API for video discovery and metadata retrieval. Utilizing official APIs provides greater stability and reliability, circumventing anti-crawling issues altogether and thereby ensuring data stability and unbiased sourcing from the outset.

---
    
**Q2:** Is it difficult to update the dataset frequently while maintaining high quality?

**A2:** We completely agree with you that maintaining consistently high data quality in a continuously updated dataset is a challenging task. However, the framework we have developed explicitly aims to systematically address this challenge.

We ensure quality at the source by collecting data from stable and authoritative international platforms, such as Forbes, BBC, CNN, as well as academic hubs like arXiv, and the world’s largest video platform, YouTube. These sources inherently provide high-quality raw materials for subsequent processing.

Our automated data pipeline deeply integrates state-of-the-art large language models (comparable to GPT-4.1) to perform critical quality-control tasks. In future annual updates, we will consistently employ the most powerful available models to ensure technical robustness and uphold our high data quality standards.

In fact, we update data continuously to ensure timeliness. Our data collection volume from May to July 2025 is shown in **Table 1**.

**Table 1: Data collection volume of the LiveVQA dataset from May 2025 to July 2025.**

|       | May | June | July |
|-------|-----|------|------|
|News   | 3301|  4021|  4391|
|Video  | 2104|  3563|  4292|
|Paper  | 1121|  1323|  1008|

---
    
**Q3:** Could relying mainly on LLM scoring (e.g., Gemini-2.0-Flash) raise concerns about the reliability and potential model bias?

**A3:** Thank you for raising concerns regarding the reliability of evaluations conducted by large language models (LLMs). As described explicitly in Section 3.1 (Evaluation) of our manuscript, to mitigate "egocentric bias," we have adopted an evaluation method identical to the widely acknowledged factuality benchmark SimpleQA. Specifically, this evaluation was conducted by Gemini-2.5-flash-Preview. Furthermore, to ensure reliability, we randomly select 300 samples, including 100 each from news, videos, and academic papers, and manually verified the results of the evaluation model. The results showed that the model achieved 100% accuracy. We believe that the model is capable of this task.

---
    
**Q4:** Are there any limitations for the data generation pipeline?

**A4:** We greatly appreciate the opportunity to delve deeper into discussing inherent challenges and limitations of our data generation pipeline. As with any sophisticated system, our pipeline indeed has certain limitations, explicitly discussed in Appendix A.

1. Current pipeline limitation to English content: The pipeline is presently tailored primarily to English content to establish a high-quality and linguistically consistent benchmark during the project's initial phase. We acknowledge that this restricts its direct applicability to multilingual scenarios. However, we are already actively expanding the framework to support 10 additional languages, and this multilingual extension is well underway.

2. Dependence on advanced APIs and associated costs: To guarantee the highest data quality, our pipeline deeply relies on advanced yet costly models, such as GPT-4.1, particularly for critical tasks like content filtering and Q&A generation. This approach inevitably incurs substantial computation and API costs. To address this, we have already migrated the pipeline to use open-source models such as Qwen3, Qwen2.5-VL, and Gemma3-27B-IT. These models have been successfully integrated into our workflow and are now operational. Our long-term goal remains to progressively adopt even more cost-effective and performant open-source models as they become available.

3. Human validation efforts for data automation: Given our extensive use of LLMs for data automation, ensuring correctness has necessitated considerable human validation efforts. As detailed in Appendix C.4, we have designed meticulous manual verification processes for each LLM-assisted step to guarantee the accuracy and reliability of generated data. While this approach effectively ensures data quality, it also imposes significant human resource costs. We continue to maintain rigorous manual validation and are committed to upholding benchmark credibility, even as we expand languages and transition to new models.

---

We hope these clarifications address your concerns thoroughly. We firmly believe that our work, through sustained commitment, provides long-lasting value to the research community. Again, we sincerely thank you for your invaluable feedback and look forward to your reconsideration in light of our detailed clarifications and future plans.

We sincerely appreciate your positive evaluation and constructive feedback. We are delighted that the reviewer regards LiveVQA as a "well-designed benchmark," capable of addressing an "important problem," and has acknowledged the quality of our experiments and the organization of the paper.

We provide detailed responses to your concerns and suggestions as follows:

---

**Q1:** whether the benchmark can be easily solved by simply including relevant recent data through more effective fine-tuning scheme？

**A1:** Thank you very much for raising this point. Indeed, as you mentioned, the improvement in model performance through fine-tuning is exactly one of our experimental findings. However, rather than indicating a limitation, this highlights a deeper challenge that our benchmark aims to measure: current methods of updating knowledge result in knowledge that is fragile and lacks generalizability. Specifically, knowledge acquired through fine-tuning proves to be brittle, as minor variations in the phrasing of questions cause a significant drop in model accuracy. For instance, a model fine-tuned to answer "Who is the person in the image?" may fail entirely if the question shifts to a different fact about the same person depicted. This demonstrates that the knowledge is superficial, not truly understood or integrated into the model’s knowledge base.
    
Moreover, fine-tuning on knowledge-rich data comes at a significant cost. Our experiments clearly illustrate this performance trade-off. As demonstrated in Figure 6 of our paper, updating models using LiveVQA data improved their performance on new knowledge but led to a notable and sustained drop in accuracy on the general visual understanding benchmark MMStar (accuracy dropped from 65.80% to 58.16%). This highlights a critical dilemma: balancing new knowledge acquisition with retention of existing capabilities is a pressing challenge in the field of knowledge updates, and our benchmark explicitly aims to measure this trade-off.

To ensure the ongoing relevance and challenge posed by LiveVQA, we deliberately designed it as a dynamically evolving benchmark and dataset with continuous updates. As we stated explicitly in Appendix A, we will annually update and release new versions of the dataset. When mainstream models' knowledge cut-off gradually overlaps with the time frame covered by the current dataset, we will publish a new version of LiveVQA encompassing entirely new content from the subsequent year. This guarantees that our benchmark consistently evaluates model capabilities beyond their current knowledge boundaries.

---

**Q2:** Could the baseline models be expanded to include newer and stronger MLLMs to better assess current capabilities?

**A2:** We agree with your suggestion that evaluating the latest models is critical to capturing state-of-the-art progress in this field. Thus, we have expanded our baseline experiments to include the most recent models—both open-source and closed-source—such as Claude4-sonnet, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking, gemma-3n-E4B-it, gemini-2.5-flash-lite-Preview-06-17, and grok4, to ensure comprehensive coverage of the latest advancements. The result is shown in **Table 1**.

The newly released models, especially Grok-4, demonstrate strong capabilities compared to their peers. This may be partly due to Grok-4’s much larger model size, which typically leads to better performance. In addition, since Grok-4 is trained on data sourced from X, it seems to have a particular advantage when dealing with real-time news content and images. This specialized training likely gives it a stronger memory for news-related visuals, further boosting its performance in these areas.

---
**Q1:** Can a continual or streaming update pipeline help keep the LiveVQA dataset relevant as MLLMs advance?

To clarify, the core contribution of our work is not merely the static, one-time LiveVQA dataset, but rather an automated framework and data engine capable of continuously generating high-quality and cutting-edge question-answer pairs. Our framework was precisely designed to systematically address your concerns about timeliness, intentionally created to be automatically streamlined and dynamically updated to integrate the latest visual knowledge.

Thus, we have expanded our baseline experiments to include the most recent models—both open-source and closed-source—such as Claude4-sonnet, GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking, gemma-3n-E4B-it, gemini-2.5-flash-lite-Preview-06-17, and grok4, to ensure comprehensive coverage of the latest advancements. The result is shown in **Table 1**. The newly released models, especially Grok-4, demonstrate strong capabilities compared to their peers. This may be partly due to Grok-4’s much larger model size, which typically leads to better performance. **Q2:** How does the dataset ensure that the crawled content truly reflects recent or ongoing events, rather than covering past topics?

**A2:** Thank you for raising a highly critical point. Regarding news articles and academic papers, we carefully extract and verify their publication timestamps. 

1. News articles were collected from authoritative news websites, while academic papers were gathered from arXiv based on the latest timestamps. Therefore, this portion of data strictly ensures its currency rather than covering outdated topics.

2. For video data, we conducted manual verification to ensure that selected content does not depict historical events, thus minimizing the occurrence of outdated content. Specifically, we manually annotated 500 data entries to verify and prevent such situations. The results show that our video data are 100% recent events, rather than old events that occurred in the past.

summary.value: This paper presents LIVEVQA, a new benchmark to evaluate how well Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) handle continuously updated visual information beyond their static training cutoffs. The dataset includes recent real-world visual content and supports studying both retrieval-based and update-based methods. The authors benchmark several state-of-the-art MLLMs and show clear gaps on post-cutoff data, while also exploring ways to efficiently update models with new visual knowledge. The dataset and code are publicly released to encourage further research.

strengths_contributions.value: This paper tackles an important problem by introducing LIVEVQA, a well-designed benchmark for testing how MLLMs handle fresh, real-world visual knowledge. The dataset’s up-to-date sources and careful validation ensure high quality, and its two-level question design effectively tests both recognition and reasoning. The experiments are solid and highlight the value of retrieval-augmented and efficient update methods. Overall, the paper is well-organized and provides clear, detailed descriptions of the benchmark’s construction and sourcing.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. The results shown in Figure 7 suggest that parameter-efficient fine-tuning significantly boosts model performance, which raises the question of whether the benchmark can be easily solved by simply including relevant recent data through more effective fine-tuning scheme.

2. The baseline models listed in Tables 2–4 could be further expanded to include more recent and stronger MLLMs or agents, such as GPT-4o-Image or other cutting-edge multimodal models, to better assess whether current state-of-the-art systems can already handle the tasks targeted by LIVEVQA.

3. Some text formatting in Table 4 appears inconsistent and should be correctted.

summary.value: This paper introduces LiveVQA—a novel dataset with 107,143 samples across 12 categories, curated from real-time sources like news, videos, and publications, to address the challenge of outdated visual knowledge in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It includes evaluations of 17 state-of-the-art MLLMs. It further investigate parameter-efficient fine-tuning, analyzing the critical trade-off between adapter capacity and model capability when integrating new visual knowledge.

strengths_contributions.value:
1. This paper is well-written and presented very clearly.
2. This paper fills the gap in the evaluation of outdated knowledge that has long been ignored in the VQA and multimodal fields, and has high practical significance.
3. The coverage and quality of the data are excellent. The dataset contains more than 107143 questions and 28488 unique images from various sources.
4. The experimental results are comprehensive, including comparisons across mainstream closed and open source mllms (GPT-4.1, Gemini, Claude, Qwen, Llama).
5. It innovatively incorporates both seeking and updating tasks into the benchmark.

limitations_weaknesses.value:
1. As new data collection is limited by platform anti-crawler and interface, the collected data may have unexpected bias.
2. It is difficult to update the dataset frequently and maintain high quality
3. The experimental part mainly uses LLM for scoring (Gemini-2.0-Flash). The reliability of LLM scoring and possible model bias may pose potential problems.
4. Are there any limitations for the data generation pipeline?

title.value: Seeking and Updating with Live Visual Knowledge

abstract.value:
The visual world around us constantly evolves, from real-time news and social media trends to global infrastructure changes visible through satellite imagery and augmented reality enhancements. However, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), which automate many tasks, struggle to stay current, limited by the cutoff dates in their fixed training datasets.
To quantify this stagnation, we introduce LiveVQA, the first-of-its-kind dataset featuring 107,143 samples and 12 categories data specifically designed to support research in both seeking and updating with live visual knowledge.
Drawing from recent news articles, video platforms, and academic publications in April 2024-May 2025, LiveVQA enables evaluation of how models handle latest visual information beyond their knowledge boundaries and how current methods help to update them. 
Our comprehensive benchmarking of 17 state-of-the-art MLLMs reveals significant performance gaps on content beyond knowledge cutoff, and tool-use or agentic visual seeking framework drastically gain an average of 327% improvement. 
Furthermore, we explore parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods to update MLLMs with new visual knowledge.
We dive deeply to the critical balance between adapter capacity and model capability when updating MLLMs with new visual knowledge. 
All the experimental dataset and source code are publicly available at: https://livevqa.github.io.

pdf.description: Upload your submission as a PDF file that ends with .pdf. In this file the main text (max. nine pages), references, and checklist may be followed by technical appendices, for which there is no page limit. Paper PDF can be updated until the full paper submission deadline (May 15).

dataset_submission.description: Indicate whether your submission includes a dataset. **If you check this box, you must provide a valid Croissant metadata file and a URL to your dataset accessible to NeurIPS2025 reviewers.** For detailed requirements, please refer to the [NeurIPS2025 data hosting guidelines](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/DataHostingGuidelines).

croissant_file.description: If you checked the Dataset Submission box, upload a Croissant metadata file that documents your dataset. If your submission has more than one Croissant metadata file, please package all files into a single ZIP archive and upload it here. **Before uploading, verify that your file is valid using the [Croissant validator](https://huggingface.co/spaces/JoaquinVanschoren/croissant-checker).** If you left the Dataset Submission box unchecked, leave this field empty.

dataset_URL.description: If you checked the Dataset Submission box, provide the URL to your dataset here. **Before including the URL for your dataset, verify that you followed the [NeurIPS2025 data hosting guidelines](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/DataHostingGuidelines) (as part of the CFPs) and that the URL is accessible to NeurIPS2025 reviewers.** If you left the Dataset Submission box unchecked, leave this field empty.

dataset_final_confirmation.description: **By checking this box, you confirm that: (1)** your dataset is complete and finalized at the time of submission; **(2)** you included a valid Croissant metadata file that has been verified using the [Croissant validator](https://huggingface.co/spaces/luisoala/croissant-checker); **(3)** you followed the [NeurIPS2025 data hosting guidelines](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/DataHostingGuidelines); **(4)** you provided a URL pointing to the dataset that is accessible for NeurIPS2025 reviewers. If you left the Dataset Submission box unchecked, leave this box unchecked.

checklist_confirmation.description: In order to improve the rigor and transparency of research submitted to and published at NeurIPS, authors are required to complete a paper checklist and include it in the paper PDF. See [https://neurips.cc/public/guides/PaperChecklist](https://neurips.cc/public/guides/PaperChecklist) and the provided 2025 sample LaTeX file. **Papers not including the checklist in the paper PDF will be desk rejected.**

code_URL.description: If your submission includes code, provide the URL to a hosting platform (e.g., Github, Bitbucket) as described in the CFPs. See the main track [code guidelines](https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy) for details.

supplementary_material.description: All supplementary material must be self-contained and zipped into a single file. Note that supplementary material will be visible to reviewers throughout and after the review period, and **ensure all your supplementary material is anonymized if your submission is anonymized.** The maximum file size is 100MB. Supplementary material can be updated until the supplementary material deadline (May 22).

financial_support.description: Optionally indicate one student author on the paper who would need financial support to attend and present at the conference if the paper is accepted (or leave blank if financial support is not needed). Please enter an email address or an OpenReview ID that exactly matches one of the authors.

reviewer_nomination.description: Every submission must nominate at least one author who is a qualified reviewer (i.e., satisfying our reviewer nomination criteria [https://blog.neurips.cc/2025/03/10/self-nomination-for-reviewing-at-neurips-2025/](https://blog.neurips.cc/2025/03/10/self-nomination-for-reviewing-at-neurips-2025/) ). Being named as such a reviewer in the submission constitutes an acceptance and a commitment to carry out the regular reviewing load (~6 papers) responsibly if asked by the PC chairs or the D&B track chairs. Only if no qualified reviewer exists in the author list, nominate the best-qualified author for consideration by the PC chairs or the D&B track chairs. In addition, note that any author listed on 4 or more papers will be automatically regarded as a reviewer unless they are already serving as a reviewer, AC, SAC, or other roles in the Organization Committee. Failure to assign a qualified reviewer when one is available in the author list may result in desk rejection. Please enter an email address or an OpenReview ID that exactly matches one of the authors (separate by comma if more than one nominations).

responsible_reviewing.description: We acknowledge that every author on the program committee is obligated to conduct responsible reviewing according to the policy designed by the PC Chairs and relevant members of the organizing committee. **Failure to do so may result in desk rejection or other serious consequences.**
